authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Editing - Formal Execution.md, §II (the typed edit taxonomy), §III (the migration predicate), §IV (the safe-change asymmetry) and §VI (edit authority — the gate on the definition); Capstone §VI.1 duty 5
note: SPEC vectors, not parity vectors. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine. The gate under test is admit(e, ⟨D,s⟩) ⟺ tok(α,e) ∧ ⊢e(D) ok ∧ Safe(e,μ) ∧ applicable(e,D).

divergence.statement: PARTIAL, and the parts differ — worth stating precisely rather than as one blanket claim.

term_by_term.tok(α,e): RUST-AHEAD. Python checks `existing["owner_user_id"] != owner_user_id` INLINE inside update_definition — that is ownership, not authority, and it never reaches admit(). No edit token exists; §VI's 'authority does not lift from below' has no representation, and a shared definition has no council-mint requirement at all.
term_by_term.⊢e(D) ok: RUST-AHEAD in scope. Python's _validate_definition_spec compiles every invariant against the candidate schema and raises on the first bad one — real, but confined to specs built through the UI, and it is not the whole-definition judgment over guards and widget bindings.
term_by_term.Safe(e,μ): AT PARITY IN SHAPE, for μ = id. Python's check_definition_edit_safety genuinely implements §III: it enumerates live instances, evaluates every candidate invariant against each instance's actual current state, and returns a witness set of {sustain_id, invariant_id, expression, reason}. It also reports an uncompilable candidate as a violation against every instance rather than skipping it. This slice matches that behaviour; it does not exceed it.
term_by_term.applicable(e,D): RUST-AHEAD. Python has no typed edit `e` at all — update_definition rebuilds a whole candidate spec from patch-or-current values and diffs nothing, so it cannot tell a DropInv from an AddInv, and §IV's free case is paid for on every edit.

divergence.when_python_catches_up: The Safe() cases are already behaviour Python exhibits and could be replayed there today if the reference grew a vector harness for definitions. The rest become parity vectors unchanged.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. This slice adds a new module and touches no existing gate path.

authority_cases.name: the_owner_of_an_unshared_definition_may_edit_it
authority_cases.why: The ordinary single-actor path. An object-level actor and a meta-level actor may coincide only here.

authority_cases.name: someone_who_does_not_hold_the_definition_gets_no_token
authority_cases.why: Holding the definition is what a sole-owner mint is FOR.

authority_cases.name: a_shared_definition_cannot_be_edited_by_one_actor
authority_cases.why: §VI's load-bearing point: authority does not lift from below. V↑ is defined over the instances, so one move in Σ↑ can affect every instance at once while a move in any single Σ affects one. Permission to spend from a pocket is not permission to redefine what a pocket is.

authority_cases.name: a_shared_definition_is_edited_by_a_council_decision
authority_cases.why: An object-level transition needs one actor; a meta-level transition needs a quorum. 'Changing the rules is harder than following them' as a structural property, not a convention.

authority_cases.name: a_council_that_did_not_pass_mints_nothing
authority_cases.why: The council advises and decides; a proposal still in voting is not a decision.

authority_cases.name: a_deferred_proposal_is_not_a_meta_level_approval
authority_cases.why: A deadline passing is not a decision — the same rule the operator-level approval token holds to.

authority_cases.name: quorum_is_required_and_is_the_composition_point
authority_cases.why: Quorum ARITHMETIC belongs to Multiparty (§4B, M-MUL) and is not built. Refusing when quorum is not asserted makes the dependency a compile-time obligation the host cannot skip, rather than a check this module pretends to perform.

token_binding_cases.name: a_token_for_one_edit_does_not_admit_another
token_binding_cases.why: The token binds to an edit, not to a right to edit. Approving 'add this floor' must not admit 'drop that ceiling'.

token_binding_cases.name: the_same_kind_with_a_different_expression_is_a_different_edit
token_binding_cases.why: Binding to the KIND would approve a shape of edit. 'Yes, add a floor at zero' must not admit a floor at fifty.

token_binding_cases.name: an_edit_approval_expires
token_binding_cases.why: The definition at approval time need not be the definition now.

gate_cases.name: dropping_an_invariant_that_does_not_exist_is_not_a_loosening
gate_cases.why: applicable(e,D). It is not a weaker rule, it is a confused edit — and only a typed taxonomy can tell the difference.

gate_cases.name: retiring_an_operator_that_was_never_declared_is_refused
gate_cases.why: applicable(e,D), transitional family. The allow-list is data in this core, so T is genuinely editable and genuinely checkable.

gate_cases.name: an_invariant_over_an_undeclared_dimension_is_a_typing_error
gate_cases.why: ⊢e(D) ok. Typing is the 'not ever' — a fact about the document, decided before anything about the instances.

gate_cases.name: retiring_a_dimension_invalidates_an_invariant_that_never_mentioned_the_edit
gate_cases.why: The reason typing is whole-definition and not a diff: RetireDim touches one line and can invalidate rules written long ago that never mentioned it. There is no local check.

gate_cases.name: an_invariant_that_will_not_parse_is_a_typing_error_not_a_skip
gate_cases.why: Fail-safe defaults. Skipping an unreadable rule is how a gate fails open.

gate_cases.name: an_edit_that_would_strand_a_live_instance_is_refused_and_names_it
gate_cases.why: Safe(e,μ) — o(s) ∈ A, a fact about the things that exist. The witness set names the instance AND the rule: a refusal that cannot say which is an alarm, not a diagnosis.

gate_cases.name: the_same_edit_succeeds_once_the_instance_is_back_inside_the_region
gate_cases.why: The refusal is about the state of the world, not about the edit. Fix the instance and the identical edit is admitted.

gate_cases.name: loosening_is_free_and_skips_the_scan
gate_cases.why: §IV's asymmetry, and the concrete payoff of having a typed `e`: a weaker V cannot strand a state already inside a stronger one, so a DropInv is admitted even against an instance that violates a DIFFERENT surviving rule — that instance was already outside, and this edit did not put it there. The reference engine pays the |inst| × |Inv| scan here because it has no `e` to classify.

gate_cases.name: a_sandbox_edit_needs_no_authority
gate_cases.why: Asking whether an edit would be safe is not permission to make it. Sandbox satisfies the authority term and nothing else.

gate_cases.name: a_sandbox_edit_is_exempt_from_authority_not_from_the_other_three_terms
gate_cases.why: Exempting the sandbox from the migration predicate is how a preview becomes a second write path.

gate_cases.name: an_edit_the_token_does_not_cover_is_refused_before_anything_else_runs
gate_cases.why: tok(α,e) is decided first: no reason to type-check an edit this actor may not make.

induction_case.name: only_gated_edits_keep_every_definition_in_V_up
induction_case.why: The meta-Sustain proposition: admit(e,·) IS §4E's gate on Σ↑, so §4E's induction applies unchanged — starting from a well-typed definition under which every instance is viable, and admitting only gated edits, EVERY definition the system ever holds has that property. Walked step by step rather than asserted.
